How do I get access to the EHR system?.answer:
To get EHR access, you'll need to submit a request [1]. Your supervisor must countersign your access request—this is a HIPAA requirement that ensures a named, accountable person authorizes your access to client information [3].

Here's what to do: submit your access request and your supervisor will receive an automatic notification. If your supervisor hasn't countersigned within 2 business days, reach out to them directly or contact it@mentella.example to escalate [3].

If you run into technical issues or have questions during the process, email it@mentella.example with your full name, regional pod, and any error message screenshots [2]. They'll help you get set up.

When is my first paycheck, and how do I.answer:
Your first paycheck arrives on the first scheduled payday after your start date [2]. Mentella pays semi-monthly on the 15th and the last business day of each month [2].

To receive it, set up direct deposit in your Paylocity profile during your first week—it's a day-1 priority [1][3]. You can add up to 3 accounts and split your pay by percentage or fixed amount [1]. Your paycheck will be deposited once you complete this setup [2].

If you start mid-period, your first check will be prorated to the days you actually worked [2]. Keep in mind that any changes to direct deposit take one full pay cycle to take effect [1].

How do I request time off?.answer:
To request time off, follow these steps [1]. First, block the dates in your Calendly calendar and either cancel or reassign any clients already scheduled during that window. Then submit your PTO request in Paylocity at least 2 weeks in advance for anything longer than a single day. Approval can be delayed if your calendar still shows open availability during your requested time off, so completing the calendar step first is important [1].

If you need same-day or next-day time off for a personal emergency, you don't need the 2-week notice—just notify your pod lead as soon as you can [1].

Where is client information allowed to l.answer:
Client information is allowed to live only in the EHR — your Electronic Health Record system [1][3]. This is the single authoritative place where any client information may be created, viewed, or stored. 

Client information must never go into email, Slack, shared spreadsheets, personal notes apps, or text messages, even when communicating with a supervisor or about scheduling [3]. If you need to flag something about a client to a colleague, use the EHR's internal messaging feature instead [3].
